title: Renewal Deck Toolkit — Standard & Enterprise Playbooks
content:
Purpose

This is a compact, reusable kit for Customer Success to run renewal-focused QBRs. Two ready-to-use deck variants are included: a concise "Standard" deck for SMB / growth customers and an expanded "Enterprise" deck for strategic accounts. The doc includes slide outlines, speaker notes, a lightweight renewal tracker, email templates, and a meeting playbook (pre/during/post).

When to use which deck
- Standard: customers with <$50k ARR, single product line, low legal/compliance friction, renewals often handled by CSM + AE. Use when the goal is to reinforce value and surface quick expansion motions. (30–45 minute meeting)
- Enterprise: customers with >$50k ARR, multiple product owners/security/stakeholders, renewal requires contracting/legal/exec sign-off. Use when you need to align cross-functional stakeholders and surface risk mitigations. (60–90 minute meeting + follow-ups)

Running the meeting (roles & timings)
- Owner: CSM runs the meeting, owns action items and tracker updates.
- Optional: AE (commercial), Solutions Engineer (technical), Customer Success Ops for contract logistics.
- Standard flow: Intro (3m) -> Health + Wins (10m) -> Usage & ROI deep-dive (10m) -> Renewal ask & next steps (7m) -> Q&A (5m) -> Close (remaining)
- Enterprise flow: Intro (5m) -> Strategic outcomes mapping (15m) -> Product adoption & blockers (15m) -> Risk & mitigation plan (10m) -> Commercial/contract path (10m) -> Exec ask (10m) -> Next steps & owners (5m)

Standard Deck (slide-by-slide, speaker notes)
1) Title + Meeting Info (1 slide)
   - Speaker note: quick hello, attendee roll-call, confirm goals for the call.
2) Meeting objectives (1 slide)
   - 2–3 bullets: why we gathered, expected outcomes (e.g., align on renewal, identify expansion).
3) One-line product value statement (1 slide)
   - Note: use the customer's own language from last call / pilot.
4) Top 3 wins since last QBR (1 slide)
   - Speaker note: metric-based where possible (e.g., latency reduced 30%, search relevance up 12%).
5) Usage snapshot + key trends (1 slide)
   - Include: MAU/DAU or API call volume, top features, performance SLOs.
6) Risk signals / open blockers (1 slide)
   - Be explicit, propose mitigation and owner for each risk.
7) Renewal ask & commercial snapshot (1 slide)
   - Current term, proposed renewal cadence, recommended SKUs/discounts.
8) Proposed success plan & next 90 days (1 slide)
   - Concrete milestones and owners.
9) Action items & owners (1 slide)
   - Assign dates.
10) Close & thank you (1 slide)

Enterprise Deck (slide-by-slide, speaker notes)
1) Title + attendees + roles (1 slide)
2) Executive summary: value realized + renewal recommendation (1 slide)
3) Strategic alignment map (1 slide)
   - Map Redwood capabilities to customer objectives (revenue ops, product ML, support automation).
4) Adoption metrics + depth of usage (2 slides)
   - Breakdown by team, endpoints, models used, regional distribution.
5) Cost/ROI model (1 slide)
   - Show token spend vs. cost savings or incremental revenue contribution.
6) Performance & reliability brief (1 slide)
   - Latency, error rates, incident history, SLO attainment.
7) Security & compliance updates (1 slide)
   - Certification status, audit notes, open infosec asks.
8) Customer success stories & concrete wins (1 slide)
9) Risks, mitigations, and support ask (1 slide)
10) Commercial proposal & renewal timeline (1–2 slides)
11) Contracting path & stakeholders (1 slide)
12) Roadmap alignment & feature requests (1 slide)
13) Open items / decision log (1 slide)
14) Action owners / milestones / escalation path (1 slide)
15) Executive ask + next steps (1 slide)

Speaker note patterns (reusable snippets)
- "What success looks like": always tie to a measurable KPI (e.g., average inference latency, time to integrate, customer support deflection).
- "If we had one ask from you": list a single exec-level decision to accelerate renewal (e.g., commit to pilot expansion or agree to timeline).
- Escalation: who to loop in for infra/ops/legal and when.

Lightweight Renewal Tracker (text table to copy into Sheet)
Columns: Customer | ARR | Contract End | Renewal Type | Renewal Owner | AE | Health Score (0-10) | Risks | Next Meeting | Action Items | Target Close Date | Contract Status
Example row (text):
Acme Corp | $72,000 | 2024-08-15 | Enterprise | Asha Patel | Jamie (AE) | 7 | Billing sync delay; security review | 2024-03-20 | Security review + PO assigned | 2024-07-01 | In negotiation

Tracker rules (operational)
- Update within 24 hours after any meeting that materially changes status.
- Health Score rubric: 8–10 green, 5–7 yellow, 0–4 red. Use adoption + exec engagement + commercial fit to calculate.
- Escalate red (<=4) to manager + solutions eng within 48 hours.

Pre-meeting checklist (CSM)
- 2 weeks before: Verify contract end date + check for overlapping procurements.
- 10 days: Run usage export, recent incidents, support ticket summary, NPS/CSAT highlights.
- 7 days: Share draft deck with AE and SE; collect any legal/compliance notes.
- 3 days: Confirm attendee list, request additional stakeholders (procurement/IT).
- 1 day: Final rehearsal, update tracker, send calendar invite with agenda and pre-read.

During meeting scripts (short prompts)
- Opening: "Thanks everyone—goal for today is to review value realized and align on next steps for renewal. We'll keep this to [X] minutes and capture action items."
- If a blocker surfaces: "I hear the blocker is X; here's our proposal for mitigation and the owner—are you comfortable with that plan?"
- When closing commercial ask: "Based on the value we've delivered and roadmap alignment, we recommend renewing for [term] with [plan]. What additional information do you need to get this approved internally?"

Post-meeting actions (24–72h)
- Update tracker and assign tasks in Jira/Linear (JIRA-RENEW-88 pattern).
- Send meeting minutes + slide deck with clear owner/due dates.
- AE to confirm commercial terms and follow up with procurement; CSM to monitor adoption action items weekly.

Email templates (short)
- Invite (subject): "Renewal QBR: [Customer] — Proposed agenda + pre-read"
  Body: "Hi [Name], attaching a short agenda and pre-read for our renewal QBR on [date]. Goal: align on value and agree next steps for renewal. Please add any stakeholders who should join (procurement, IT, exec)."

- Post-meeting summary (subject): "[Customer] — QBR notes & next steps (owner + due dates)"
  Body: "Thanks for the time today—attached are the slides and the actions we captured. Owners and due dates are in the tracker; flag anything that looks off and we'll update immediately."

Commercial negotiation quick tips
- If the customer asks for a discount, trade for a commitment (longer term, volume, or public case study).
- Document concessions in the tracker and make them contingent on signature by agreed date.
- When procurement delays: get a verbal buy-in and lock a provisional PO if possible.

Common escalation triggers (auto-escalate to manager)
- Health score drops by >=3 points within 30 days.
- Security/compliance blocker unresolved for >14 days.
- AE unavailable for >10 days during a critical renewal window.

Open questions / TODOs in this doc
- Should we include a cost-savings slide template for customers who use hybrid (Dedicated + Hosted) setups? (Action: Marco to prototype two variants)
- Legal: template clause for early renewal incentives — attach to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-12345. (Action: Evelyn to confirm)
- Deck assets: create a small slide library with visuals (usage heatmaps, adoption waterfall) — design ask. (Action: Liam)

Quick change log
- 2024-02-12: initial draft created (Asha).
- 2024-02-19: added enterprise commercial negotiation section (Marco).
- 2024-02-28: updated tracker example and added post-meeting checklist (Evelyn).

Notes to self
- Keep the Standard deck <10 slides; customers appreciate brevity.
- For enterprise customers, schedule a separate legal/contract touchpoint outside the QBR when contract complexity is high.

If you reuse any slide, change the data placeholders and always validate with SE for technical accuracy.

End of doc
